newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek banks buy 450 mln ecus, 100 mln marks at fix.
newsitem.headline: Greek banks buy 450 mln ecus, 100 mln marks at fix.

text.p: Greek commercial banks bought about 450 million ecus and 100 million marks for drachmas at the central bank's fixing, state and foreign bank dealers said.

About 500 million dollars in spot and six-month forex swaps were bought earlier during intraday trading prompting the central bank to intervene by selling dollars for drachmas, dealers at foreign banks said.

Some dealers attributed the outflows to profit taking and position squaring by foreign players, especially a Zurich-based Swiss bank and a London branch of another Swiss bank. Others said there was a speculative element related to snap elections.

"The foreign players reversed positions," said a forex dealer at a foreign bank. "There is speculation that the race between the socialists and conservatives is getting tighter than many of us think."
Greece is to hold national elections on September 22.
